kill_argument: The strongest objection is that an effect for a synthetic voluntary-training cohort cannot answer the historical program question advertised by the title, and observational adjustment cannot itself recover causality. I attacked that scope and the claimed novelty: plan.json explicitly restricts the contribution to a synthetic evaluation exercise conditional on identification assumptions, and makes no new-method or historical-effect claim. I also checked the Imbens/Xu abstract and Lakens primary PDF against the recorded positioning; they support the stated cautions. The remaining question-level defects are ambiguous population wording and a title that drops the synthetic qualification. Neither defeats the explicitly conditional, falsifiable ATT exercise. The equivalence bound still requires its promised prospective scale justification at design review. No data, estimates, models or answer keys were inspected or run.

findings.text: The question uses “Among enrolled adults” without explicitly distinguishing program participants from all cohort members. H1 and the contribution specify ATT, but the question wording could also be read as defining a sample restricted to participants. State the target as the average treatment effect on program participants in the supplied cohort, using eligible nonparticipants as the observational comparison. Resolution requires consistent estimand/population wording in the question and later design; no new experiment is needed.
findings.response: Designer clarified plan.json question and design.data/estimand to target participants ATT with cohort nonparticipants as comparison; clarification preserves approved scope. No outcome values inspected.

findings.text: The project title omits synthetic status and can be read as an empirical evaluation of a historical training program. The narrower contribution in plan.json is defensible only if that qualification survives into the title and paper framing. Add synthetic evaluation/exercise to the title; resolve with consistent title and contribution wording.
findings.response: Designer updated crew.json title to explicitly identify a synthetic cohort; design summary/data and existing contribution retain synthetic evaluation framing. No historical-effect claim added.
